**TCP vs. UDP – the two most common transport‑layer protocols**

| Feature | **TCP (Transmission Control Protocol)** | **UDP (User‑Datagram Protocol)** |
|---------|------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| **Connection model** | Connection‑oriented – a three‑way handshake (SYN‑SYN‑ACK‑ACK) establishes a logical session before data is exchanged. | Connection‑less – each datagram is sent independently; no handshake is required. |
| **Reliability** | Guarantees delivery. Lost, duplicated, or corrupted segments are detected (via checksums & sequence numbers) and retransmitted. | No reliability guarantees. Lost or corrupted packets are simply discarded; the application must handle any recovery. |
| **Ordering** | In‑order delivery. Sequence numbers let the receiver reorder out‑of‑order segments before passing data up the stack. | No ordering. Packets may arrive in any order, or not at all. |
| **Flow control** | Uses a sliding‑window mechanism (receiver advertises how much data it can accept) to avoid overwhelming the receiver. | No flow‑control mechanism; the sender can flood the network or the receiver. |
| **Congestion control** | Implements algorithms (e.g., Reno, CUBIC, BBR) that throttle the sending rate when network congestion is detected. | No congestion control; the sender transmits at whatever rate the application dictates. |
